response.rationale: Chronic periventricular white matter changes point to small vessel disease, which best explains the persistent wide-based unsteadiness, positive Romberg, and mild central dysmetria. Vestibular and vertebrobasilar causes are actively excluded by the HINTS/algorithm, normal TCD hemodynamics, and absence of recent ischemic lesions.

rejected.why: Carotid plaques and tortuosity are present, but stenosis was overestimated and cerebro-afferent hemodynamics were normal, making atherosclerosis an unlikely active cause of the episodes.

Upright unsteadiness could suggest orthostatic intolerance, but there are no orthostatic vital signs, no clear lightheadedness/presyncope pattern, and the prolonged episodes lasting days to weeks are atypical.
Recurrent vertigo and movement-provoked dizziness are suggestive, but the diagnostic algorithm and negative HINTS argue against a central or peripheral vestibular origin.
Vertebrobasilar insufficiency is excluded by normal TCD hemodynamics of cerebro-afferent vessels and no recent posterior circulation ischemic lesions on MRI.
Cerebrovascular disease is not supported as the active diagnosis because repeat MRI showed no recent vascular lesions and there are no new focal deficits.
Cervical vertigo lacks supporting cervical spine findings, neck pain, or a clear head/neck movement-specific trigger in the vignette.
